findings.title: 'Always show yourself' does nothing on the default profile (maxRows=0): the pin works against a 40-row cap, but the window draws only about 10 rows
findings.evidence: ApplyRowLimit treats cap<=0 as Const.MAX_ROWS (40), while Render stops at layout.maxRows (10 at 220px). The pin also ignores the scroll offset. Headless repro: 'default window: maxRows=0 alwaysShowSelf=true visible=10 kept=20 self-in-view=false' (player at rank 15). The existing test covers only an explicit maxRows=3.
findings.remediation: C-02: add a pure, allocation-free Aggregator.SelfPinIndex(entries, first, visible, rowsConfig) beside ApplyRowLimit. Window:Render computes the pin index for 1+offset and layout.maxRows (skipped in drill-down) and draws entries[pin] in the last slot. Keep ApplyRowLimit's pin. Keep Render at CCN 15 or below with a single-expression substitution or a named local, never a part2 split. Pass the entry's real rank if the name cell shows one. Tests: 3 in tests/test_window.lua (default window with player at rank 15; scrolled so the player is in the slice; alwaysShowSelf=false) and 1 in tests/test_aggregator.lua. Smoke test SM-04.
findings.verify_reason: Aggregator.lua:1291-1311 maps maxRows<=0 to Const.MAX_ROWS (40, Constants.lua:616) and pins the player at rows[40]. Window.lua:328-335 rowCapacity derives layout.maxRows from the frame height, and Render at Window.lua:1206-1207 stops at layout.maxRows starting from 1+offset. No other pin exists in Window*.lua (grep for isPlayer). Defaults.lua:281 has alwaysShowSelf=true, so on the default profile a player ranked past the visible rows is never pinned. In raids this is common and silent, so high stands. The remediation is sound.

findings.title: A disabled addon re-shows its windows when Test mode is unticked, because WindowProto:Show() skips the latch
findings.evidence: The guard at :659 checks only NS.Perf.suspended (the perf hold) and never NS.IsStoodDown(). WindowProto:Show() calls frame:Show() without consulting NS.ShouldShow. Headless repro: 'windows shown while disabled after test-mode on/off: 1 / 1'. The window stays up because every event is unregistered.
findings.remediation: C-01: WindowProto:Show() returns false first when NS.IsStoodDown(). Change WindowManager.lua:659 to use `not (NS.IsStoodDown and NS.IsStoodDown())`. Test in tests/test_disabled.lua: disable mid-session, tick and untick Test mode, and assert no window is shown ('red under' reverting the Show() guard). Keep test_lifecycle.lua:288 and Disabled 5 green. Smoke test SM-01.
findings.verify_reason: WindowManager.lua:659 passes keepShown = not enabled and not NS.Perf.suspended, so it never checks NS.IsStoodDown(). applyTestMode (:630) then calls inst:Show(). Window_Placement.lua:231-242 WindowProto:Show() calls frame:Show() and sets forcedShow with no latch check. The settings panel's state.testMode setter (Schema_Compose.lua:794-801) reaches M:SetTestMode while disabled. NS.IsStoodDown (LifecycleSetup.lua:270) covers both the disabled hold and the perf hold, so the proposed :659 change subsumes the current perf check. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: Chat exports call the deprecated global SendChatMessage from a feature module, and would silently fall back to printing to self
findings.evidence: `local send = chatType and _G.SendChatMessage`. The global has been deprecated since 11.2.0 (Deprecated_ChatInfo.lua) in favour of C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage. When it is absent, the export prints the lines to the player and returns true, with no notice, so a channel export looks sent when nothing was sent.
findings.remediation: C-03: add Compat.ChatSender() in core/Compat.lua, resolved at call time, preferring C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage and falling back to _G.SendChatMessage. Export.lua uses NS.Compat.ChatSender(). If a real channel was requested and no sender exists, print one localized notice before the self-print. SELF stays silent. Tests (tests/test_export.lua): C_ChatInfo preferred; one notice on RAID with no sender; no notice on SELF. A LibKa0s-Compat member is deferred (one consumer, anti-pattern #55). Smoke test SM-05.
findings.verify_reason: Export.lua:879 does `chatType and _G.SendChatMessage` in a feature module, and :885-889 silently self-prints when it is absent. compat.md:5/25 does make Compat.lua the only file allowed to call deprecated APIs, so the deviation is real. Severity is lowered to medium: the global still resolves through Blizzard's deprecation fallbacks today, so no export fails now. The silent fallback is a future-removal risk, not live breakage. The remediation is fine.

findings.title: During a perf capture's suspended arm, /mm toggle and the launcher's left-click still show windows
findings.evidence: Feature verbs are refused only while disabled. Under the perf hold, Toggle calls inst:Show(), which bypasses the ladder. Headless repro: 'windows shown during perf suspend after /mm toggle: 1 / 1'. This contaminates arm B of the capture.
findings.remediation: C-01: the Show() latch guard, plus M:Toggle returning false with L['Windows are suspended while a performance capture runs.'] when NS.IsStoodDown(). The launcher (LauncherSetup.lua:235-236) prints that err. Add the locale key. Test in tests/test_disabled.lua: under a perf suspend, toggle and launcher onClick show nothing and print the line. Smoke test SM-02.
findings.verify_reason: The Slash gate asks only NS.IsDisabled (Slash.lua:254; the comment at :150 says so), and the launcher's onClick (LauncherSetup.lua:229-237) does the same. Under a perf suspend, M:Toggle (WindowManager.lua:690-708) calls inst:Show(), and Show() bypasses NS.ShouldShow's step-0 latch. That puts a shown, redrawing window into the suspended arm, against performance-§6. The remediation is correct. Using IsStoodDown for the refusal while keeping the IsDisabled-based gate wording separate matches the design in LifecycleSetup.lua:277.

findings.title: A window created while the addon is stood down is armed with an OnUpdate
findings.evidence: Window.New calls inst.frame:SetScript('OnUpdate', onUpdate) unconditionally. Create and Duplicate are reachable from the settings panel while disabled. Reproduced headless: the OnUpdate is left armed.
findings.remediation: C-01: arm OnUpdate only when not NS.IsStoodDown(). Stand-up already re-arms it via WindowManager:Resume. Test: Create while disabled leaves no OnUpdate, and after enable every instance has one. Smoke test SM-03.
findings.verify_reason: Window.lua:1382 arms OnUpdate unconditionally in Window.New, and Create/Duplicate (WindowManager.lua:253, :341) can call it while stood down. That breaks slash-commands.md:190/279 ('no new one is armed for the rest of the run'), so the finding is real. Severity is lowered because RefreshVisibility at :1383 hides the frame (ShouldShow step 0), and WoW does not fire OnUpdate on a hidden frame. There is no CPU cost unless something shows the frame, which is R-02/R-04's defect. It is a standards deviation with nil reachable impact once C-01 lands. The remediation is fine.

findings.title: The Slash degradation stub has no DisabledLine, and the launcher calls it through an always-present wrapper
findings.evidence: The wrapper `function Sl:DisabledLine() return cli:DisabledLine() end` always exists, so the launcher's guard passes and the stub raises 'attempt to call method DisabledLine' on a disabled left-click. This is reachable only when Launcher loads and Slash does not.
findings.remediation: C-04: publish Sl:DisabledLine only if cli.DisabledLine exists. Do not add a separate stub wording. Test in tests/test_degraded.lua: remove LibKa0s-Slash from libFiles, disable, call the launcher onClick, and assert no error and no write. Optionally note the coverage in test_surface_parity's header. Smoke test SM-11.
findings.verify_reason: The stub's SlashLib:New (Slash.lua:185-236) builds no DisabledLine. The wrapper at :743 always exists, so the launcher's `Sl.DisabledLine` guard (LauncherSetup.lua:232) passes and cli:DisabledLine errors. That is real. It is reachable only when the vendored LibKa0s-Slash fails to load while the Launcher loads, and the addon is disabled, and the player left-clicks. That is a degradation-path edge case, so low rather than medium. The remediation is fine.

findings.title: Every refresh releases and rebuilds every visible row, and Row:Update writes hidden cells
findings.locations: modules/Window.lua:1168; modules/Window.lua:912-914; modules/Window.lua:1206-1220; modules/Row.lua:1446-1455; modules/Row.lua:1199-1204; modules/Row.lua:1376-1378
findings.evidence: HideAll releases the pool and Cell:Clear clears each cell. Rows are then re-acquired, re-anchored and refilled 4 times a second in combat. Capture 20260909-014604 (dated, solo): render 0.75 ms/pass, renderRow 0.10 ms/row. Offline refresh20x7 is 1.31 ms/iter. The saving is unmeasured.
findings.remediation: C-05 (measure first): keep self.slots bound across passes, acquire only when needed, release only the surplus, and re-anchor only when layoutVersion (bumped in ApplyConfig) changes. For Row:Update, make ApplyLayout keep an ordered array of live cells on the row (self.liveCells, rebuilt only in ApplyLayout, reusing the table rather than allocating a new one each call). Row:Update then iterates that array instead of pairs(self.cells). The alternative is to iterate layout.columns and index self.cells. Row.lua must stay at or under 1500 lines. Gate: before and after in-client /mm perf bundles (SM-07) with render ms/call lower. Offline refresh20x7 must keep API count at 8 and bytes/iter at or under 303438.1. Revert if render does not move.
findings.verify_reason: The churn is real: Render calls HideAll -> Pool.ReleaseAll -> Row:Release, which clears every cell (Row.lua:1446-1455, Window.lua:912-914, :1168). Row:Update also iterates pairs(self.cells) (Row.lua:1376-1378), including cells that ApplyLayout hid. The remediation's reference to an existing `self.live` is wrong, though. `live` is a per-call local in RowProto:ApplyLayout (Row.lua:1311-1326) and is never stored on the row. The saving is also explicitly unmeasured and gated on in-client captures, so low rather than medium. Row.lua is currently 1469 lines, which leaves 31 lines of headroom under the 1500 cap.

findings.title: The remembered roster (db.global.roster) is persisted with no bound and is never cleared at login
findings.locations: modules/Roster.lua:355-361; modules/Roster.lua:572-582; modules/Roster.lua:621; modules/Roster.lua:628-630; modules/Roster.lua:489; modules/Roster.lua:506; modules/Roster.lua:519
findings.evidence: Every build() records each member into seenMap.byGuid, which is cleared only by Roster.Forget on METER_RESET. IsGroupMember falls back to the remembered map, so players from earlier sessions may pass the group filter. Unverified: whether DAMAGE_METER_RESET fires at login.
findings.remediation: C-14, blocked on smoke test SM-06. If the meter is empty after a fresh login, call Roster.Forget() on ENTERING_WORLD with isLogin. If the data survives logout, cap the map (for example, prune entries not in the live roster above 4 x MAX_ROWS). Add a case in either branch. No SavedVariables write from a game event while disabled.
findings.verify_reason: Roster.lua:355-361 copies each member into db.global.roster.byGuid. That map is cleared only by Roster.Forget (:572-582) on METER_RESET (:621, :628-630), and IsGroupMember/OwnerOf fall back to it (:506, :519). So the map is persisted with no bound, as stated. The impact is speculative, though. A remembered GUID matters only if it appears in the current C_DamageMeter session data, which is group-scoped. Growth is bounded by the players you grouped with between meter resets. The finding itself says the login behaviour is unverified and blocks on SM-06. That makes it SavedVariables hygiene at low, not medium. The remediation, conditional on SM-06, is sound.

findings.title: Visibility:Evaluate runs the whole ladder to feed a LastResult cache that no shipped code reads
findings.evidence: Visibility.LastResult has zero callers in core/, modules/ or settings/. Only a test reads it. Each window's rules are evaluated twice per context edge, with a table allocated per changed result.
findings.remediation: C-06: return early from Evaluate when not State.debug, and delete Visibility.LastResult and its test (or wire it into /mm debug diag). Keep the subscriptions.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Visibility.lua:373 defines LastResult. A grep of core/, modules/ and settings/ finds no caller, and only tests/test_visibility.lua:451,459,493,498 read it. Evaluate (:389-419) runs ShouldShow for every window and allocates a table in remember() on each change. It does this on ZONE, ENTERING_WORLD, ROSTER, COMBAT and PLAYER_STATE edges (:461-471), and modules/Window.lua:1292-1313 subscribes to the same edges and runs the ladder again. Evaluate publishes nothing, so outside debug the pass has no effect. Side note: core/LifecycleSetup.lua:102-106 says standDownVisibility's Refresh is 'the pass that asks them [windows] to go', but Evaluate hides nothing. That comment is wrong whether or not this fix lands. Callers ignore Refresh's return value (LifecycleSetup:106,173, Schema_Compose:58), so an early return is safe.

findings.title: Window commands answer with the wrong error string
findings.locations: modules/WindowManager.lua:704; modules/WindowManager.lua:272; modules/WindowManager.lua:307; modules/WindowManager.lua:309; modules/WindowManager.lua:324; modules/WindowManager.lua:471-472; locales/enUS.lua:901
findings.evidence: /mm toggle <unknown> answers 'Setting not found: %s'. /mm window delete|copy <unknown> answers 'No window is selected.' An empty rename answers the label L['Window name'].
findings.remediation: Same as C-07, with rule_ref cleared: this is not a localization-§2 deviation.
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. modules/WindowManager.lua:704 returns L['Setting not found: %s'] for an unknown toggle name. Delete :272 and CopyFrom :471-472 return 'No window is selected.' for an unknown name, and Slash.lua reaches these through WINDOW_VERBS (Delete(tail), CopyFrom(source,target)). Rename :309 returns L['Window name'] for an empty name. The rule_ref is wrong, though. These strings are already routed through L, and localization-§2 (English source-of-truth keys) is met. This is a wrong-message UX defect with no standards rule behind it, so rule_ref should be empty.

findings.title: Feature-verb acknowledgements are raw English strings, with a concatenated plural
findings.locations: settings/Slash.lua:415; settings/Slash.lua:428; settings/Slash.lua:446-447; settings/Slash.lua:580; settings/Slash.lua:632-633; settings/Slash.lua:696-697
findings.evidence: These lines are unrouted, while the same file routes NS.L["No window named '%s'."] at :574. The plural is built by concatenation.
findings.remediation: C-08: route the cited lines through NS.L with whole-sentence English keys and format placeholders, using two keys for the 1/N windows plural. Do the same for the other unrouted user-facing lines in settings/Slash.lua (:193, :207, :232, :367, :556, WINDOW_USAGE). Add every key to locales/enUS.lua and leave no enUS key unread. Cite localization-§1 (routing SHOULD), not §2/§3. Smoke test SM-09.
findings.verify_reason: The cited raw strings exist: settings/Slash.lua:415 (lock), :428 (test), :446-447 (reset positions, where the plural is built by concatenating '1 window'/'N windows'), :580, :632-633 (feign) and :696-697 (tooltip). :574 routes NS.L. The rule refs are wrong. The routing SHOULD, and the note that concatenated sentences are unroutable, are in localization-§1. §2 covers English keys, and §3 covers enUS coverage plus the English-only register. MultiMeters has no documented-deviation row that puts it in the English-only state (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:414 only mentions 'English only' as a ceiling), so the SHOULD is open. The same file has more unrouted user-facing lines that the finding misses: :193/:207 (version), :232 ('unknown command'), :367, :556 and WINDOW_USAGE at :453-455.

findings.title: The drill-down closes when its window is renamed
findings.evidence: The drill-down exits on any WINDOWS_CHANGED addressed to its window, including action 'renamed'.
findings.remediation: C-13: exit only when payload.action ~= 'renamed'. Add a case in tests/test_drilldown.lua. Smoke test SM-10.
findings.verify_reason: DrillDown:OnWindowsChanged (modules/DrillDown.lua:850-855) exits any view whose id matches payload.windowId, whatever the action. WindowManager:Rename announces (cfg.id, 'renamed') at :316, so renaming a drilled window closes its drill-down even though its data and columns have not changed. Excluding 'renamed' is correct. findings.title: UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED and CHAT_MSG_SYSTEM stay registered all session for narrow uses, and neither is measured
findings.evidence: No perf bucket brackets either handler, so their cost is unverified.
findings.remediation: C-15, measurement only: add the handlers to an existing bucket or a debug-only counter. A new bucket needs its descriptor entry in core/PerfSetup.lua and its bracket in the same commit. Decide on registration changes next cycle from the numbers.
findings.verify_reason: core/MultiMeters.lua:201 and :208 register both events in OnEnable for the whole session. The comment at :196-199 calls UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED 'the busiest thing this addon listens to'. core/PerfSetup.lua:103-122 declares no bucket covering OnSpellSucceeded or OnSystemMessage, and only the DAMAGE_METER handlers (:419-432) carry a Perf bracket. performance-§3 says hot-path handlers SHOULD be bracketed and that every declared bucket must be reached, which matches the remediation (declare the bucket and add its bracket in the same commit). Both handlers return early, so the impact is unmeasured cost, not a known cost. Low and measurement-only is right.

findings.title: 28 LibKa0s tags (v1.18.0 to v1.53.0) were vendored with no re-vendor bundle and no register row
findings.evidence: The commits name 34 distinct tags since the 2026-08-25 horizon. The bundles name 8 tags (v1.15.0, v1.25.0, v1.30.0, v1.31.0-v1.34.0, v1.55.0). The kit-only v1.54.2 (d2169d4) is not seen by the check. The High comes from AUDIT.md step 4; by player impact this would be Low.
findings.remediation: Write one consolidated bundle, docs/revendor/<date>-v1.34.0-to-v1.54.2/ (or widen it to v1.15.0 -> v1.54.2, or add a second bundle for v1.15.0 -> v1.30.0). Its 01_DELTA.md first line names the span, and 05_SUMMARY.md records the carrying commit and any adoption per tag. Do not back-fill a folder per tag. Any later collection re-vendor writes its own bundle.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (A re-vendor commit implies a bundle); AUDIT.md step 4
findings.verify_reason: I read the CLAUDE.md provenance line at each of the 39 commits since 2026-08-25 that touch libs/LibKa0s. Together they vendor 34 distinct tags, v1.18.0 through v1.55.0. The docs/revendor bundles, read from their folder names and 01_DELTA.md first lines, record v1.15.0, v1.25.0, v1.30.0, v1.31.0-v1.34.0 and v1.55.0. That leaves 28 tags unrecorded, matching the finding. ARCHITECTURE.md has no deviation row. audit-review-history ('A re-vendor commit implies a bundle') is a MUST, AUDIT.md:341-347 sets it at High, and the same rule says one consolidated bundle naming the span discharges the backlog, which is what the remediation proposes. The severity follows the playbook, and the evidence already notes that player impact is low.

findings.title: Event registration is not isolated per event, and rejected names are not recorded
findings.evidence: There are 21 bare self:RegisterEvent calls, so the first unknown name aborts every later one, including DAMAGE_METER_*. registerIfValid calls RegisterEvent outside the pcall. The :153-156 comment wrongly says an unknown event costs nothing. Nothing reachable by the player records rejections.
findings.remediation: Add a single pcall-wrapped registerEvent(target, event, handler) with IsEventValid as a front gate, and route all 22 registrations through a module-level EVENTS list. Keep failures in NS.State.rejectedEvents, reset on each OnEnable, with a debug line. Show them in /mm debug diag. Add a test_lifecycle case using M.__badEvents. Fix the comment and add a note in docs/midnight-quirks.md. Keep target=self so Disabled 3 and Disabled 9 stay green.
findings.verify_reason: I counted 21 bare self:RegisterEvent calls in core/MultiMeters.lua:134-215. registerIfValid (:124-132) calls target:RegisterEvent outside the pcall once IsEventValid passes. The :153-156 comment claims an unregistered-namespace event 'costs nothing', which is wrong, because an unknown name raises. Nothing in core, modules or tests references rejectedEvents or __badEvents. events-frames-taint-§1 ('An unknown event name raises...') has three MUSTs: per-event pcall isolation, recording the rejected names, and making that record reachable by the player. The kit mock supports M.__badEvents (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725), and Disabled 3 and Disabled 9 exist in tests/test_disabled.lua:166 and :456, so the remediation is sound. On the current client every name is valid, so Low fits the reachable impact.

findings.title: Tag 1.0.1-release ships a TOC saying 1.0.0, with no Version History row and no release run

findings.title: Three Tier 2 docs are owed (slash-dispatch.md, message-bus.md, profiles.md), and their register rows falsely say 'Not applicable'

findings.remediation: Spill the Slash commands, Message bus and Profiles material into the three canonical docs (a move, with a summary and link left in the hub). Flip the rows to Present, and keep test_docmap and test_doc_structure green. Do this after the code sprints.
findings.verify_reason: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:475-477 marks slash-dispatch.md, message-bus.md and profiles.md 'Not applicable'. documentation-§3's Tier 2 table (documentation.md:251-255) says each MUST ship when its trigger holds: 8 or more commands or any subcommand tree (the row itself says 18 verbs plus the window tree), more than 10 messages (the row says 14), and user-visible profiles (settings/Profiles.lua:80 registers the AceDBOptions table as an options page). The rows justify the gap with 'fits in a screen', which the rule does not accept, and none of the three docs exists under docs/. It is a docs-only gap, so Low.

findings.title: Three closed issues carry an open-state label (#4, #21 state:triaged; #24 state:untriaged)

findings.title: British 'minimise'/'minimised' survives in player-visible strings, README, identifiers and comments, held by an unsanctioned waiver
findings.locations: locales/enUS.lua:214; locales/enUS.lua:231; README.md:50; modules/HeaderControls.lua:127; tests/prose_waivers.lua:24; tests/prose_waivers.lua:30-57
findings.evidence: 154 lines across 22 authored files. The waiver covers 25 files and calls itself 'a DEBT, not a decision'. None of the three sanctioned waiver shapes applies, and there is no register row.
findings.remediation: Correct prose, comments, README (with the de-AI pass) and locale values. Rename the keys (L['Show minimize'], L['Minimized']) and the header control key and art together with all call sites. Remove each minimis waiver entry in the same change, and delete the file if it ends up empty. Stored paths go through MM-A-18a. Afterwards grep minimis returns 0 in authored scope.
findings.verify_reason: The British spelling is in the cited places: locales/enUS.lua:214 L['Show minimise'] and :231 L['Minimised'], README.md:50, and modules/HeaderControls.lua:127 (key, setting and art). tests/prose_waivers.lua:30-57 waives minimis across 25 files, and its own header calls this 'a DEBT, not a decision'. localization-§5 allows a waiver only for a spelling that is 'not the repository's English to correct', and names three shapes: a library field name, a game-data token, and a generated client dump. This is the repo's own spelling, so the waiver is unsanctioned. My grep of authored scope counts 173 lines across 27 files versus the stated 154 across 22, because I included docs/superpowers and the generated test-cases. That difference does not change the finding. Low is right.

findings.title: The minimise spelling reaches two stored SavedVariables paths, so it needs a v15->v16 migration (derived from MM-A-18)
findings.evidence: showMinimise=true and window.frame.minimised=false are stored keys. A find-and-replace would orphan every player's stored values.
findings.remediation: Add a v15->v16 step in the Database runner that walks every profile and window, copies minimised->minimized and showMinimise->showMinimize, then nils the old keys. Rename defaults and schema rows, keep ValidateSchema passing, and add a migration case. Alternatively, ratify the decline as a localization-§5 register row.
findings.verify_reason: defaults/Profile.lua:130 has showMinimise=true and :148 has minimised=false, and both are stored SavedVariables keys. The waiver header confirms that settings/Schema.lua references the path. The last migration in core/Database.lua is migrations[14] (:904), so the schema is at v15 and the next step is v15->v16, as proposed. versioning-git:8 requires a schemaVersion bump whenever a SavedVariables migration is needed. The remediation (walk every profile and window, copy the value to the new key, nil the old key, and add a test) is correct. Its alternative, a register row, is also a valid documentation-§3 route.

findings.title: Three load-bearing TOC positions carry no at-line comment, and conventional groups have no 'conventional' marker

The :128-131 comment mentions OptionsSetup only as a consumer of Schema_Paths. No group carries a 'conventional' note. The dependencies are real. settings/OptionsSetup.lua:378/505 publishes NS.Helpers, and settings/General.lua:61 captures it at file scope. core/PerfSetup.lua:96 calls NS.Version() in the descriptor at file scope. core/CoreSetup.lua:55 defines NS.LIBKA0S_MISSING, which DebugLogSetup.lua:253 and LauncherSetup.lua:109 read. toc-file.md:136-160 matches the claim: an unannotated load-bearing line is a MUST failure, and the conventional note is a SHOULD. anti-patterns #66 cites toc-file-§5. findings.title: 57 citations do not parse as filename-§N (space form, §-less form, literal \194\167 in comments), including a register Rule cell

findings.title: ka0s-bounded is installed at ~/.claude/wow-addon/bin but is not on PATH
